newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Basis bids steady-firmer.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Basis bids steady-firmer.

text.p: Basis bids for dark northern spring wheat were steady to firmer on Friday, boosted by a pickup in both domestic and export-related demand and the current slow pace of farmer sales, dealers said.
"We've had a little more demand from the domestic flour mills and some export business. A few guys (producers) are selling but not many. Most farmers are in the fields," one Montana dealer said.
MGE July spring wheat futures closed four cents a bushel higher at $4.15-1/4 while cash basis bids were raised by up to nine cents.
Weather in North Dakota and Montana continued to be largely favorable for planting spring wheat.

Dealers in Montana said most farmers in the state had either finished planting or would have done so by the end of the weekend. USDA reported earlier this week that Montana was 62 percent planted, as of last Sunday.
